title: Shoes and hats off
body: Remove shoes and hats at Buddhist sites, often for the whole compound including the stupa terraces, not just the shrine room. Stone gets hot by midday, so plan early visits or carry socks.

title: Cover shoulders and knees
body: Modest clothing is expected at temples. White or light clothing is traditional, especially on poya days, but it is not mandatory.

title: Face the Buddha
body: Don't pose for photographs with your back to a Buddha image, and don't climb plinths or use statues as props. Avoid pointing the soles of your feet at Buddha images or monks.

title: Keep it on your right
body: Walk clockwise around stupas and bodhi trees, so the monument stays on your right-hand side.

title: Step around moonstones
body: Moonstones are part of a sacred threshold: walk around rather than over them where you can; many are roped off.

title: Ask before you photograph
body: Ask before photographing people, rituals or monks, and respect no-flash rules where they apply. At Sigiriya, photographing the frescoes is not allowed.

title: At Hindu kovils
body: Some inner shrines are closed to non-Hindus. Men may be asked to remove their shirts at some kovils, so follow the signs and what others around you are doing.

title: Buddha tattoos
body: Tattoos of the Buddha are regarded as disrespectful in Sri Lanka, and travellers with visible ones have been refused entry or deported. Keep them covered, and check current official advice before you travel.
